answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
Benefits:

Consequential accounting is the only method that measures the actual emissions impacts of corporate actions. Unlike attributional/inventory methods, which allocate usage rather than measure impact, a consequential method adapts to grid realities and, if properly structured, assesses how consumption and procurement decisions affect system-wide emissions.

A well-designed consequential framework would provide effective market signals that incentivize companies to manage emissions from their operations and guide procurement toward the most impactful projects for decarbonization. The data infrastructure to accurately measure marginal emissions rates by location already exists in broad measure and continues to expand both in the US and internationally.

Challenges:

The most significant challenge with the current proposal is that it measures avoided emissions only, without accounting for induced emissions based on consumption. Both induced and avoided emissions are necessary to understand the net impact on system-wide emissions resulting from corporate actions. Without visibility into both sides of the equation, it is not fully clear which actions have the greatest net impact. The proposed formula closely resembles existing project accounting, which has had limited adoption in this context because it does not provide a complete picture.

For consequential accounting to be meaningful, it must be recognized as a primary or co-equal metric within Scope 2 reporting and be suitable for target-setting. If relegated to supplemental disclosure, it will not change procurement behavior or provide a genuine alternative to attributional methods. We are also concerned that managing consequential accounting under a separate work stream (AMI) with an uncertain timeline risks delaying or deprioritizing it relative to the MBM revisions. Publication and effective dates for Scope 2 and AMI must be coordinated to ensure companies can evaluate the full range of compliance pathways.

Additionality tests must also balance credibility with feasibility and establish appropriate reasonableness thresholds. Financial additionality stemming from long-term procurement that enables financing for greenfield and re-power projects should offer an explicit method for demonstrating additionality. On the other hand, if additionality tests are overly stringent, this could potentially deter investment in impactful projects.

answers.label: Appropriateness of the TWG subgroup formula
Why the formula is or is not appropriate
answers.text: The formula needs to measure emissions impacts from BOTH procurement and consumption.

answers.label: Why secondary effects should be excluded
answers.text: Primary effects only which are measurable and avoid potential double counting.

answers.label: Why annual or lifetime reporting
answers.text: Electricity grids and generation resources change over time. Therefore, the emissions impacts of procurement and consumption should be continually measured on an ongoing basis.

answers.label: Requiredness of the financial analysis test
Requiredness of the common practice test
Why selected tests should be included
answers.text:
Actions should meet regulatory and timing tests as well as either (i) financial analysis, (ii) positive list, or (iii) contractual/tenor tests to be considered additional. Regulatory and timing tests weed out claims where it can be easily demonstrated that the action by itself did not influence the ultimate emissions impact. Supplementing these with either a financial, positive list or contractual/tenor test provides additional validation that the action was additional.

We believe a contractual/tenor option should be available, but should not rely on tenor alone (e.g. a minimum percentage threshold of a project's total capacity, as well as a minimum tenor). Even in cases where it could be argued that a project's fundamentals could justify its development in the absence of (for example) a long-term offtake agreement, entering into such a contract often carries material risk and significantly improves a project's bankability and capital efficiency.
